Fix: Add multilingual support for Google ASR including Korean (#461)

* fix: add multilingual support for Google ASR including Korean

This commit addresses issue #359 by expanding language support in the
Google ASR integration. Previously, Korean and several other widely-used
languages were missing from the language code mapping, causing them to
fall back to English.

Changes:
- Added Korean (ko-KR) language support
- Added Spanish (es-ES), Italian (it-IT), Portuguese (pt-BR)
- Added Russian (ru-RU) and Arabic (ar-SA) support
- Updated both google_asr.py and google_asr_rtsp.py
- Created comprehensive multilingual documentation
- Added test suite for language support validation

This fix enables users to configure OM1 agents to recognize speech in
their native language without requiring English. The implementation
maintains backward compatibility with existing configurations while
expanding accessibility for international users.

Testing notes:
- All new language codes follow Google Cloud Speech-to-Text standards
- Default fallback to English remains unchanged
- Case-insensitive and whitespace-tolerant language names

Hot-reload and configuration management (#642)

* hotload feature

* Add hot reload tests for CortexRuntime and ModeCortexRuntime

Introduces comprehensive test cases for hot reload functionality in both single and multi mode Cortex runtimes. Tests cover initialization, file modification detection, config reload success and failure, orchestrator stopping, and cleanup logic, ensuring robust coverage for dynamic configuration reloading.

* Enable hot-reload by default in Cortex runtimes

Changed the default value of the hot_reload parameter to True in both multi_mode and single_mode Cortex runtime classes. Updated docstrings to reflect the new default behavior, making hot-reload enabled by default for configuration files.

* Track and manage cortex loop task lifecycle

Introduces explicit tracking of the cortex loop task in both multi-mode and single-mode runtimes, ensuring proper cancellation and cleanup during shutdown and config reloads. Updates tests to mock the cortex loop task where appropriate. Also sets hot_reload default to True in run.py.

* Improve orchestrator shutdown and reload handling

Refactors orchestrator shutdown logic in both multi_mode and single_mode cortex runtimes to use asyncio.wait with timeouts, improving robustness during hot-reload and mode transitions. Adds a reload-in-progress flag to prevent ticks during reload, enhances logging for task cancellation, and updates tests to mock asyncio.wait instead of gather.

* Enhance cortex runtime orchestration by skipping sleep during shutdown and ensuring proper task management

* Remove unnecessary logging in the cortex loop to streamline execution

* Implement runtime config hot-reload for multi and single mode

Adds a runtime configuration file mechanism for both multi_mode and single_mode runtimes to support hot-reloading. The runtime config file is now generated and monitored for changes, triggering reloads from the original config source. Refactors config loading functions to accept an optional source path, updates manager and cortex logic to use the runtime config, and adjusts tests to mock the new behavior. Also updates state file naming for clarity.

fix: resolve WebSim event loop conflict in Docker environments (#1643)

* fix: resolve WebSim event loop conflict in Docker environments

The tick() method crashed with "This event loop is already running"
when deployed in Docker containers, causing WebSocket state updates
to fail and frontend to display "OM Agent Status: OFF".

Root cause: Attempting to call run_until_complete() on an already
running event loop (e.g., when uvicorn server is running).

Solution: Check if the event loop is already running using
loop.is_running(). If so, use asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe()
to safely schedule the coroutine from the synchronous thread.
Added a 1-second timeout to prevent blocking forever.

Also removed the fallback loop.create_task() which was ineffective
since the created task was never awaited.

Closes #1621

fix: properly filter blanked RPLidar angles using any() in _path_processor (#2141)

* fix: use any() to properly filter blanked RPLidar angles in _path_processor

Closes #2138

The angle blanking logic in _path_processor used a `continue` inside a
nested `for b in self.angles_blanked` loop (lines 453-457). That
`continue` only skipped to the next blanked range in the inner loop
instead of skipping the outer `for angle, distance in data` iteration.
As a result, readings from blanked angles were never actually filtered
and always reached `complexes.append(...)`, sending phantom obstacles
from fixed chassis reflections to the path planner.

Replace the nested loop with `any(b[0] <= angle <= b[1] for ...)` which
evaluates the blanking check as a single expression. When a match is
found, the outer loop's `continue` fires correctly, skipping the
reading. This approach:

- Fixes the control flow bug in one line
- Short-circuits on the first matching range (same as break)
- Matches how rptest.py already handles blanking correctly (lines 276-282)

Add two tests exercising _path_processor directly:
- test_path_processor_filters_blanked_angles: verifies readings inside
  [-170, -150] are excluded while readings outside pass through
- test_path_processor_no_blanking_when_empty: verifies no readings are
  lost when angles_blanked is empty

Affected configs: turtlebot4.json5, turtlebot4_lidar.json5,
turtlebot4_lidar_gps.json5, test_lidar.json5 — any robot with
non-empty angles_blanked was seeing phantom obstacles.
